stem: The jejunum predominantly occupies which region of the abdomen:
fact: The jejunum is located mainly in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen.
finding: NCBI states that the jejunum is located mainly in the abdomen's left upper quadrant.

stem: A 64 year old man is brought to ED with profuse haematemesis. Endoscopy shows oesophageal varices which are most likely the result of anastomosis of the left gastric vein with which of the following vessels:
fact: The left gastric vein forms a portosystemic anastomosis with oesophageal veins draining to the azygos system at the gastro-oesophageal junction.
mnemonic: Left gastric meets oesophageal veins, then azygos.
sourceLabel: PMC: Collateral Pathways in Portal Hypertension
finding: The source and PMC review support the azygos system as the caval-side partner of the left gastric vein in oesophageal varices.

stem: The superficial inguinal ring is an 'opening' in which of the following structures:
fact: The superficial inguinal ring is a triangular opening in the external oblique aponeurosis.
finding: NCBI describes the superficial ring as a triangular opening made by fibres of the external oblique.

stem: The supraduodenal region of the common bile duct:
options: lies superior to the cystic duct.
lies in the free margin of the greater omentum.
lies to the left of the hepatic artery proper.
lies anterior to the portal vein.
empties into the major duodenal papilla.
fact: The supraduodenal common bile duct lies in the free margin of the lesser omentum and is anterior to the portal vein and right of the hepatic artery proper.
mnemonic: Portal triad order: bile duct anterior, portal vein posterior.
finding: NCBI places the common bile duct with the portal triad; the source explanation specifies that the supraduodenal CBD is anterior to the portal vein and right of the hepatic artery proper.

stem: The abdominal aorta bifurcates into the right and left common iliac arteries at which of the following vertebral levels:
fact: The abdominal aorta bifurcates into the right and left common iliac arteries at L4.
sourceLabel: NCBI Bookshelf: Posterior Abdominal Wall Arteries
finding: NCBI states that the abdominal aorta branches into the right and left common iliac arteries at L4.

stem: Regarding the rectus abdominis muscle, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: It originates from the pubic crest, pubic tubercle and pubic symphysis.
It inserts onto the costal cartilages of ribs 5 - 7 and to the xiphoid process.
It is separated in the midline by the linea alba.
The free lower border of its aponeurosis forms the inguinal ligament.
It is intersected along its length by tendinous intersections.
fact: The inguinal ligament is formed by the free lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis, not the rectus abdominis aponeurosis.
finding: NCBI identifies the inguinal ligament as a thickened inferior portion of the external oblique aponeurosis; this supports the source's incorrect statement.

stem: The quadrate lobe of the liver lies between which of the following structures:
options: Ligamentum teres and inferior vena cava
Ligamentum venosum and inferior vena cava
fact: The quadrate lobe is on the inferior liver surface between the gallbladder and the fissure for the ligamentum teres.
finding: NCBI places the quadrate lobe lateral to the round ligament and closely associated with the gallbladder; the source explanation specifies the fissure for ligamentum teres.

stem: The obturator nerve is formed from the anterior rami of:
fact: The obturator nerve arises from the anterior rami of L2–L4.
finding: NCBI states that the obturator nerve arises from the second through fourth lumbar roots.

stem: The uterus receives its blood supply primarily from which of the following blood vessels:
options: Uterine branches of the ovarian artery
Uterine artery from the internal iliac artery
Uterine branches from the internal pudendal artery
Uterine branches from the umbilical artery
Uterine branches from the median sacral artery
fact: The uterine artery, a branch of the internal iliac artery, is the main uterine blood supply; it anastomoses with the ovarian artery.
mnemonic: Uterine artery: internal iliac, then crosses the ureter.
finding: NCBI states that the uterine artery is a branch of the internal iliac artery and that its ascending branch anastomoses with the ovarian artery.

stem: The pancreas occupies which of the following abdominal regions:
fact: The pancreas lies in the epigastric region and left hypochondrium and extends transversely between the duodenum and spleen.
finding: NCBI places the pancreas transversely in the upper abdomen between the duodenum and spleen; the source explanation specifies epigastrium and left hypochondrium.
